(group MY1980-optugu) [claude-code/opus]

records.actors: Royal Malaysian Navy; Attorney-General's Chambers (prosecution); Ministry of Foreign Affairs
records.suggestion_reasoning: Detention and prosecution of another claimant's nationals in disputed waters, followed by a formal warning to their government, is coercive (physical interference plus a threat of legal punishment), and the first such action against Filipinos found. The date and location come from Lim (2000) and Dzurek (1996), both PDFs; the checked first source (Hansard, 11 November 1988) describes the prosecution and warning but not the date; Hansard of 29 November 1988 places the detention in the Spratlys. Manila protested and the case strained relations through late 1988. [confidence: high]

records.summary: On 4 April 1988 the Royal Malaysian Navy seized three Philippine fishing boats near Commodore (Rizal) Reef and detained their 49 crew, who were charged under Malaysia's fisheries law with fishing without permission in its EEZ; after a Kota Kinabalu Sessions Court freed them the prosecution appealed, then withdrew at Manila's request, and Malaysia formally told the Philippine government to warn its fishermen to respect the Malaysian EEZ or face full legal action, while stating it did not recognise the boundary claimed by the Philippines.
records.presort: new move (novelty) — Novelty: seizure, prosecution and a formal warning to Manila over Philippine boats near Commodore Reef; 1987's record has no coercive act (nothing comparable). Lead of the 1988 Spratly fisheries-enforcement move; Hansard detention counts (3 Philippine boats 1986, 5 Vietnamese 1986-87) are unlocated and could show earlier enforcement. (group MY1988-enforcement) [claude-code/opus]

records.summary: On 29 June 1988 the Government, replying in the Dewan Rakyat committee stage of the supplementary development estimates, said that the Department of Fisheries had completed studies of tuna and seaweed resources at Swallow Reef showing potential for tuna fishing, that it would issue licences to qualified applicants to fish in the reef's waters, and that $358,000 was sought to expand research facilities on the reef.
records.presort: continuation of ev-7d4224d75d (a candidate, provisional) — Licensing tuna fishing and expanding research at Swallow Reef implements 1987's deep-sea fishing initiative ev-7d4224d75d at the same level. Provisional on 1987 being decided. [claude-code/opus]
